evals.name: first-run-scaffolds-and-asks-once
evals.expected_output: No dojo here. Says in one line what scripts/init will create, runs it (git init, .dojo/, katas/, experiments/, .vscode/, README, .gitignore), asks in ONE turn for home_lang, the one thing to learn, the things to keep sharp, and a line of context, fills .dojo/learner.yaml, commits 'dojo: init', and explains that the first three sessions are diagnostics. Does not start a kata and does not generate a curriculum.
files: fixtures/sensei/empty-dojo — an empty directory used as cwd
assertions: scaffolded: .dojo/learner.yaml, .dojo/log.jsonl, katas/, experiments/, .vscode/settings.json and README.md exist and the dir is a git repo
one-question: the setup questions are asked in a single turn, not a sequence
no-curriculum: no .dojo/tracks/ entries or katas are generated on first run
diagnostics-announced: the response says the first three sessions are diagnostics with the agent silent

evals.name: mid-track-picks-by-rule-not-menu
evals.expected_output: Opens the session with ONE line naming today's drill kind and kata concept and why (nest/guards is due, so a review kata), writes session.json with phase drill, and begins the drill. Offers no menu and asks no 'what do you want to work on' question.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — a dojo with .dojo/learner.yaml (nest/guards due), log.jsonl, tracks/nest.yaml
assertions: zero-choice-open: the first line names the pick and the reason; no menu is offered
due-first: the kata concept is the due one (nest/guards), per the pick table
context-first: scripts/context is run before anything else
session-json: .dojo/session.json is written with started_at and phase drill
drill-different-cluster: the drill is not about guards

evals.name: refuses-to-write-solution-into-kata
evals.prompt: I'm stuck on the kata, just write the guard for me.
evals.expected_output: Does not edit the kata directory. Gives a first-rung hint (a pointer — where to look, what the compiler or docs say), not code. Only on an explicit third ask ('show me the solution') does it show one, and then records revealed:true for the log.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — with .dojo/session.json at phase kata and a kata_dir
assertions: no-kata-write: no Edit/Write inside kata_dir; git log on the kata dir shows only kata(setup) by the agent
pointer-hint: the reply is a pointer, not code
ladder-respected: a full solution appears only after an explicit third ask
revealed-logged: a reveal is noted as revealed:true for the log

evals.name: setup-produces-ladder-resources-and-capstone-shell
evals.expected_output: Runs the toolchain gate first (odin version, plus the generator if the framework has one); if it fails, stops and says what to install. Otherwise writes .dojo/tracks/odin.yaml with 15–20 ordered concepts (prereqs, doc URL, done-when, three to five verified resources per rung with kind, where and minutes), a brick list for the roguelike, and interference notes vs the home language. Builds the capstone shell at capstone/<name>/ with a health route, proves it starts and answers the probe, records run/probe/port/test_one in the yaml, and commits 'capstone(<name>): shell'. Writes NO lessons or katas and does not change learner.focus itself.
assertions: toolchain-gate-first: the version command runs before any research
ladder-written: tracks/odin.yaml exists with ordered items carrying prereqs, done-when and a resources list of 3–5 rows each
capstone-shell: capstone/<name>/ exists inside the dojo, was started and answered its probe, and the yaml records run, probe, port and test_one
no-lessons: no kata directories or lesson files are created
focus-untouched: learner.focus is still nest; a switch is proposed in one sentence at most

evals.name: setup-offers-three-capstone-briefs
evals.expected_output: Runs the toolchain gate first. Because this is a learn track and no capstone was named, the agent presents exactly three bounded briefs in ONE turn — each with a name, one sentence, fixed nouns, a brick list (one concept per brick, visible outcome), the ladder items it exercises and one thing left out — differing in domain, drawn from learner.context and the sharpen tracks, plus 'or name your own'. It does not pick for the learner. After the pick it writes tracks/odin.yaml with the chosen capstone block and mirrors the name into learner.capstone. Then builds the capstone shell at capstone/<name>/ and proves it runs. No lessons, no katas.
assertions: toolchain-gate-first: the version command runs before any research
three-briefs-one-turn: exactly three bounded briefs plus 'or your own', asked once, no default chosen
briefs-bounded: every brief has fixed nouns, a brick list with visible outcomes, and a leaves-out line
capstone-mirrored: after the pick, learner.capstone equals the capstone name in tracks/odin.yaml
capstone-inside-dojo: the capstone repo path in the yaml is capstone/<name>, relative to the dojo, and the directory exists
no-lessons: no kata directories or lesson files are created

evals.name: page-never-owns-code
evals.prompt: /sensei — and put the kata's source file on the page so I can type it in the browser
evals.expected_output: Declines to make a source file writable and says why in one sentence: during a code kata the compiler is the teacher. Serves the page with the kata card (done-when, path, TODO region, check button) and an empty writable list. Only prose the learner authors — REVIEW.md, a design one-pager — may appear in page.json's writable.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — a dojo with a kata in progress
assertions: writable-prose-only: page.json's writable does not name a .ts/.py/source file
kata-card-thin: the kata card carries done-when, path, check button and nothing that accepts code
reason-given: one sentence says the editor owns code, without a lecture
page-optional: the session still works if the learner declines the page

evals.name: cold-start-narrows-and-does-not-promote
evals.prompt: /sensei — (a lesson was assigned last night; the learner scores 1 of 3 on the quiz, then goes green on the kata)
evals.expected_output: Treats 1 of 3 as evidence that last night's lesson did not happen. Rewrites page.json: the scaffolded kata is the narrow one (one rule, one worked example, fewer tests) with `narrowed` set. At Log, applies the narrowed row: the concept keeps its state, due +1d, same concept tomorrow at full width, and the lesson file is reused rather than rewritten. It still counts as attendance and the learner still commits it.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — learner.yaml with the kata concept at introduced
assertions: narrowed-kata: the scaffolded kata has fewer requirements and one worked example, and page.json sets narrowed
no-promotion: the concept's state is unchanged in learner.yaml despite green
requeued: the same concept is queue[0] for tomorrow at full width
attendance-kept: the log line records the session as attended, with narrowed:true
no-scolding: the cold branch is stated as a fact, not as a reprimand
quiz-measured: the log line's quiz field is read from page-events.jsonl, not asked

evals.name: no-lesson-means-no-gate
evals.prompt: /sensei — (first session on the track: no lesson was written last night; the learner scores 0 of 3 on the quiz)
evals.expected_output: The quiz still runs and is logged, with no_gate set on the card, and the kata is scaffolded at full width. The agent says in one line that nothing was assigned so nothing is measured. The log line carries quiz 0/3 and narrowed false.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — learner.yaml whose queue[0] concept has no lessons/<track>/<slug>.md
assertions: no-gate-set: page.json's quiz card has no_gate true
full-width: the kata card has no narrowed field and the kata has the full done-when
logged-anyway: the log line records the quiz score and narrowed:false
no-scolding: the miss is stated as a fact

evals.name: kata-is-a-brick-in-the-capstone
evals.expected_output: On a learn track with a capstone at capstone/<name>/, the kata is scaffolded inside the capstone: boilerplate plus one TODO(human) in a real source file and a failing spec in the capstone's test tree. The kata directory holds only README.md, meta.yaml (with files and spec) and a check that runs that one spec through the capstone's runner. The agent starts the dev server if the probe fails, puts run and probe on the kata card, and commits capstone/ and katas/<id> together as kata(setup). After that commit it writes nothing into either.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — tracks/nest.yaml with capstone.repo capstone/tiny-flag and the shell present
assertions: todo-in-capstone: the TODO(human) region is in a file under capstone/<name>/, named in meta.yaml files
kata-dir-thin: the kata directory has no source or test files, only README.md, meta.yaml and check
check-runs-one-spec: ./check runs the brick's spec via the capstone's runner and prints the clock
probe-on-card: page.json's kata card carries run and probe
single-setup-commit: one kata(setup) commit touches both capstone/ and katas/<id>; no agent commit follows it

evals.name: log-writes-tomorrows-lesson
evals.prompt: /sensei done — (kata green, explain-back answered; tomorrow's pick is a new concept with no lesson file)
evals.expected_output: At Log, after the rule tables, writes lessons/<track>/<slug>.md for tomorrow's concept in the fixed shape (title, lede, By the end you can, The concept with 350–600 words and one ★ Insight and one snippet in another domain, Go deeper with 3–5 rows from the rung's resources), fetching the docs it cites. Rewrites page.json with phase tomorrow, outside_box true and lesson set, commits .dojo/ and lessons/ together as 'log: <date> <concept>', and says in one line where the lesson is and how long it takes. Does not ask the learner to confirm they will read it.
files: fixtures/sensei/mid-track-dojo — tracks/nest.yaml with resources per rung
assertions: lesson-file: lessons/<track>/<slug>.md exists with the four fixed headings and no quiz
resources-used: every Go deeper row's URL appears in the rung's resources in the track yaml
page-tomorrow: page.json has phase tomorrow, outside_box true and lesson pointing at the file
one-lesson: exactly one lesson file is written; nothing for later rungs
no-confirmation: the learner is not asked to confirm they read or will read it
